# atoom, vendored

[atoom](https://github.com/truvity/atoom) holds the ports, drivers and kits that sluis shares with session and ritueel. sluis's own contracts import atoom's messages (`proto/sluis/store` imports `atoom/common/v1alpha1/common.proto`), and sluis hosts the drivers of its key port (`atoom/key/v1alpha1`) of its item port (`atoom/store/v1alpha1`) of its source port (`atoom/source/v1alpha1`) and of its four audit ports (`atoom/blob/v1alpha1`, `atoom/transport/v1alpha1`, `atoom/index/v1alpha1`, `atoom/destination/v1alpha1`), so the proto files of atoom are copied here, unchanged, at the release named in [PIN](PIN). Nothing here is edited by hand.

- `proto/`: the proto files of every atoom port, from `<port>/proto/atoom/` at the pinned release. `buf` reads them as a dependency; they are not an output (`buf.gen.yaml` leaves them out), because the generated Go comes from atoom's own modules, `github.com/truvity/atoom/<port>`, which `go.mod` requires. The Go package of each file is set in `buf.gen.yaml` (managed mode) to that module's `gen` directory.
- `versions.yaml`: atoom's pinned runtimes at that release. `just atoom-check` holds this repository's ConnectRPC, Protobuf and buffa pins to it, as the plan says: atoom bumps first, then the consumers.
- `PIN`: the source, the version, the tag, the commit the tag names, and the sha256 of the files above.

The Rust side takes the crates of atoom that sluis uses as git dependencies at the same release tag (`[workspace.dependencies]` of the root `Cargo.toml`): `atoom-common` (the refusal helpers) and, for the item port, `atoom-store-rqlite` (the rqlite driver's library, which `drivers/store/rqlite` hosts), `atoom-store-memory` and `atoom-store-conformance` (the in-memory engine, the rules store@'s tests share and the suite, which the rqlite host's `conformance` command runs), `atoom-socket` (the client the tests dial with, and the dial and call context of exporter@'s client of a destination driver) and `atoom-store` (the contract, for the tests that call a driver directly). For the source port it takes `atoom-source-file` (the file driver's library, which `drivers/store/file` hosts and `store check --validate` reads a directory with) and `atoom-source-credential` (the credential driver's library, which `drivers/store/credential` hosts), and `atoom-source` (the contract, for the tests that call a driver directly). For the audit ports it takes `atoom-blob-fs` (the fs blob driver's library, which `drivers/writer/fs` hosts), `atoom-blob-fsreadonly` and `atoom-blob-fsdir` (the read-only driver and the directory code both share, which `drivers/indexer/fs` hosts), `atoom-transport-spool` (the spool, which `drivers/writer/spool` hosts), `atoom-index-sqlite` (the sqlite index driver, which `drivers/indexer/sqlite` hosts, and the tests of the indexer and the reader), `atoom-destination-dir` (the directory driver, which `drivers/exporter/dir` hosts), `atoom-destination-conformance` (the service, the in-memory driver and the suite; exporter@'s tests and the directory host's use them) and the contracts `atoom-blob`, `atoom-transport`, `atoom-index` and `atoom-destination` (for the tests that call a driver directly). `atoom-destination` is also the port crate that holds the `Destination` trait, `Document`, `Error` and the address rules, with no digest, command line or socket host in its dependencies: exporter@ takes them from it, and so it takes the client, `atoom_destination::client::Client`, which it builds over `atoom_socket::dial` and makes its calls with in an `atoom_socket::call::scope` (the deadline and a correlation id of its own go out on each call); it keeps only its own SHA-256 (`actors/exporter/src/digest.rs`). atoom's conformance kits for its drivers (`source-conformance`, `blob-conformance`, `transport-conformance`, `index-conformance`, `store-conformance`, `destination-conformance` and the key kit) run in atoom's CI, not here (decision D4 A of atoom's plan: atoom is low level; sluis runs its product conformance, the OpenID plans, and a new atoom is the trigger to run them again). `just atoom-smoke` runs one short smoke test for each host of a driver (the tests named `the_atoom_driver_smoke_...` and `TestAtoomDriverSmoke...`): the host starts the driver behind its guarded socket and one round trip comes back. The hosts' `conformance` commands, which an operator can run against a driver, stay. `sluis-proto` also generates the vendored messages (`connectrpc-build` cannot point a message at another crate), so it holds a second, wire-identical copy of `Refusal`, `IndexEntry`, the item, source, blob, transport, index and destination messages, which store@, the audit actors and exporter@ speak through; the helpers of the refusal detail come from `atoom-common`.

To move to another release: `just atoom-sync X.Y.Z` (needs the network; it resolves the tag `vX.Y.Z` of atoom to its commit and sets `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the vendored files and the PIN; running it again changes nothing), then `just proto-gen`, and commit everything. `just atoom-check` (in `just check-rules`; it needs the GitHub API and fails closed) fails when the version differs between `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml` and the PIN, when a `replace` of an atoom module appears, when a vendored file changed, when the tag no longer names the pinned commit, and unless atoom's CI job `check` is green on that commit. The pin is a release tag, never a bare commit: `go.mod` requires `vX.Y.Z` of every atoom module directly and `Cargo.toml` has `tag = "vX.Y.Z"` (Cargo.lock holds the commit the tag names). The PIN records `version`, `tag`, `commit` and `sha256`. Pinned now: `v0.3.0`.

- `testdata/slotplan-vectors.json`: the vectors of the slot map check of `github.com/truvity/atoom/key/slotplan`, which the Rust twin of that check (`actors/store/src/config/slotplan.rs`) reads, so that both implementations are held to one file. It is part of the PIN's digest.
